entries.name: Buttermilk
entries.role_in_recipes: Adds acidity and tenderness; its acid activates baking soda for lift.

subs.name: Milk + lemon juice or vinegar
subs.use: 1 Tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar + enough milk to reach 1 cup; rest 10 min
subs.function_note: The acid curdles the milk, mimicking buttermilk's tang and soda-reactivity.

subs.name: Plain yogurt, thinned
subs.use: 3/4 cup plain yogurt + 1/4 cup milk, whisked smooth
subs.function_note: Cultured yogurt carries the same lactic acid tang.

subs.name: Soy or almond milk + acid
subs.use: 1 Tbsp lemon juice or vinegar + enough soy or almond milk to reach 1 cup; rest 10 min
subs.function_note: The acid curdles plant milk the same way.

subs.name: Milk + cream of tartar
subs.use: 1 3/4 tsp cream of tartar + enough milk to reach 1 cup
subs.metric_use: 8 g cream of tartar + 240 ml milk
subs.function_note: Cream of tartar is a dry acid — same reaction, no added flavor.

entries.name: Eggs
entries.role_in_recipes: Binds, leavens, adds moisture and structure; sets when heated.

subs.name: Flax egg
subs.use: 1 Tbsp ground flaxseed + 3 Tbsp water; rest 10 min until gelled
subs.function_note: Ground flax mucilage gels like egg white.
subs.tradeoffs: Binds but doesn't leaven; bakes denser

subs.name: Water + oil + baking powder
subs.use: 1 1/2 Tbsp water + 1 1/2 Tbsp oil + 1 tsp baking powder
subs.metric_use: 22 ml water + 22 ml oil + 4 g baking powder
subs.function_note: Oil adds the moisture; baking powder supplies the lift.

subs.name: Unsweetened applesauce
subs.function_note: Pectin and fiber bind moisture.

subs.name: Aquafaba (chickpea liquid)
subs.use: 3 Tbsp aquafaba (2 Tbsp in place of 1 egg white); whips to peaks
subs.function_note: Chickpea cooking water carries proteins that whip like egg white.
subs.tradeoffs: Whips faster but is less stable than whites

subs.name: Plain yogurt
subs.function_note: Yogurt adds moisture and binding; no leavening.

entries.name: Butter
entries.role_in_recipes: Adds fat, flavor, and lift (creamed with sugar); browns and crisps.

subs.name: Olive or vegetable oil
subs.function_note: Oil is 100% fat vs butter's ~80%.
subs.tradeoffs: Cookies spread more; cakes moister but less airy; no butter flavor

subs.name: Coconut oil
subs.use: 1 cup coconut oil, solid (refined for neutral flavor)

subs.use: Replace up to HALF the butter with applesauce (1/2 cup butter = 1/2 cup applesauce)

subs.function_note: Pectin holds the moisture fat would.
subs.avoid_if: cookies, pie crust, or anything that needs creaming for lift
subs.tradeoffs: Denser and very moist; less richness

subs.name: Vegan butter / margarine

subs.name: Ghee

subs.name: Chilled coconut cream
subs.function_note: High fat traps air once chilled and whipped.

subs.name: Half-and-half + butter
subs.function_note: Same fat math as milk plus butter.

entries.name: Milk

subs.name: Soy or oat milk

subs.name: Water + butter

subs.name: Evaporated milk, diluted

entries.name: All-purpose flour

subs.name: Bread flour
subs.use: 1 cup bread flour — use slightly less liquid in the recipe
subs.function_note: Higher protein builds more gluten.

subs.name: Cake or pastry flour
subs.function_note: Lower protein makes less gluten.

subs.name: GF 1-to-1 baking blend
subs.use: 1 cup blend that contains xanthan gum
subs.function_note: Xanthan gum mimics gluten's binding.

entries.name: Cake flour
entries.role_in_recipes: Low protein (~8%) for tender, fine-crumbed cakes.

subs.name: AP flour + cornstarch
subs.use: 1 cup minus 2 Tbsp AP flour + 2 Tbsp cornstarch; sift twice
subs.function_note: Cornstarch dilutes AP's protein, limiting gluten.

entries.name: Bread flour
entries.role_in_recipes: High protein (~12-14%) develops strong gluten for chewy, tall breads.

subs.name: All-purpose flour
subs.function_note: AP's lower protein makes less gluten; knead 1-2 min longer.

subs.name: AP flour + vital wheat gluten
subs.use: 1 cup AP flour + 1 tsp vital wheat gluten
subs.function_note: Vital wheat gluten restores the protein gap directly.

entries.name: Self-rising flour

subs.name: AP flour + baking powder + salt
subs.use: 1 cup AP flour + 1 1/2 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp fine salt, whisked
subs.function_note: It is the same blend, made fresh.

entries.name: Baking powder
entries.role_in_recipes: Double-acting leavener: rises when wet AND when heated.

subs.name: Baking soda + cream of tartar
subs.use: 1/4 tsp baking soda + 1/2 tsp cream of tartar
subs.function_note: Cream of tartar is the dry acid that reacts with soda on contact.
subs.best_for: Batters headed straight to the oven

subs.name: Baking soda + acid in the recipe
subs.use: 1/4 tsp baking soda + swap the recipe's liquid for buttermilk or yogurt
subs.function_note: Buttermilk or yogurt supplies the acid the soda needs.

entries.name: Baking soda
entries.role_in_recipes: Base that reacts with recipe acids (buttermilk, brown sugar, yogurt) for lift.

subs.name: Baking powder (triple the amount)
subs.function_note: Powder carries its own acid; soda is 3-4x stronger.
subs.safety_note: Soda is 3-4x stronger than powder and needs recipe acid. Trippling powder adds a salty, metallic taste and less lift; best only in strongly acidic batters.

entries.name: Brown sugar

subs.use: 1 cup white sugar + 1 Tbsp molasses (2 Tbsp for dark)
subs.function_note: Brown sugar IS white sugar plus molasses.

subs.use: 1 cup white sugar (result is crisper, less chewy)
subs.function_note: Molasses is what makes brown sugar soft and acidic.
subs.tradeoffs: Crisper, less chew, no caramel note

subs.name: Coconut sugar
subs.function_note: Unrefined cane sugar with natural molasses.

subs.name: Muscovado sugar
subs.function_note: Even deeper molasses — the connoisseur's brown sugar.

entries.name: Powdered sugar
entries.role_in_recipes: Finely ground sugar with cornstarch; dissolves instantly in frostings and glazes.

subs.name: Granulated sugar + cornstarch, blended
subs.use: 1 cup granulated sugar + 1 tsp cornstarch; blend until fine powder
subs.function_note: Blending fractures the crystals; cornstarch prevents caking.

entries.name: Honey

subs.name: Maple syrup

subs.name: Light corn syrup

subs.name: Honey

subs.name: Golden syrup

entries.name: Molasses

subs.name: Dark corn syrup

subs.name: Brown sugar + water

subs.name: Black treacle
subs.function_note: The British twin — slightly more bitter.

entries.name: Cornstarch

subs.name: Arrowroot powder

subs.function_note: Different starch chemistry — sets at a lower temperature.
subs.tradeoffs: Clearer, glossier; breaks if boiled hard

subs.name: Tapioca starch
subs.function_note: Same pure-starch behavior with more elasticity.

subs.name: All-purpose flour
subs.use: 2 Tbsp flour; cook 2-3 min longer to lose the raw taste
subs.function_note: Flour is only part starch — the rest is protein.
